source.title: Poisoning the Genome: Targeted Backdoor Attacks on DNA Foundation Models
source.authors: Charalampos Koilakos; Ioannis Mouratidis; Ilias Georgakopoulos-Soares

record.tranche_reason: The study tests targeted data-poisoning attacks on DNA models, not whether standard deep networks fit completely random training labels or how they generalize on them.
record.gate_note: The study's targeted BRCA1 label-flipping experiment reports classification outcomes that relate to label corruption but do not test any listed version. Its sequence backdoor results concern trigger-conditioned generation and do not test the claim.
record.test_reason: The study measures deliberately installed sequence backdoors and held-out classification AUROC after domain-specific label flipping. The deep backbone in the classification experiment is frozen; only an L2-regularized logistic regression classifier is trained. No experiment reports training-set fitting of random labels, unstructured inputs, or the learning order of real versus noisy labels.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that targeted poisoning can install conditional generation backdoors during genomic-model pretraining or LoRA fine-tuning, and that targeted label corruption can degrade downstream classification on frozen model embeddings, motivating provenance tracking, integrity verification, and robustness evaluation.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses targeted sequence backdoors and domain-specific label flipping in genomic models; it does not reproduce the random-label fitting methods in the original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: The label-poisoning outcome varies with the fraction of BRCT labels flipped and with which domain is poisoned; sequence backdoor activation also varies by trigger, model, and tokenizer.

fits_no_version.finding: BRCT AUROC decreases from 0.849 to 0.415 as the fraction of BRCT labels flipped increases from zero to all. Full BRCT poisoning leaves RING AUROC at 0.791 and lowers global AUROC from 0.886 to 0.661. Full RING poisoning lowers RING AUROC to 0.649 and BRCT AUROC to 0.789.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Domain-targeted label flipping can selectively degrade held-out variant classification by a logistic regression classifier trained on frozen genomic-model embeddings, including below-chance discrimination in the targeted BRCT domain.

record.problems: The authors state that experiments cover Evo 2 and GENERator and that generalization to future models remains to be determined. BRCT label-poisoning confidence-interval values are not given in the supplied text, only the use of 95% intervals across 10 seeds.
record.rows_left_out: Sequence-trigger backdoor-generation results are omitted because they do not measure fitting random labels or the listed claim versions. The supplementary figure-only variant probability plots are also omitted; the text provides the relevant AUROC outcomes.

untested.parts: Deep-network training error and chance-level test performance under completely random training labels with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative training time for true and random labels, and convergence speed as label corruption increases.
Zero training error on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training-set fitting and steadily worsening test error under random label corruption across the full dataset. Domain-targeted flipping and held-out AUROC alone do not establish this.
Whether explicit regularization prevents random-label fitting, and whether removing regularization harms generalization on true labels.
Whether shared real-data patterns are learned before noisy labels. Backdoor activation over an escalating poison schedule does not measure this learning order.

record.verdict_notes: All recorded AUROC values and baselines match the supplied text. Random selection of variants for binary label flipping within a chosen domain is not complete random labeling of the training set. Evaluation uses out-of-fold predictions against original labels and does not measure reproduction of corrupted training labels. Sequence-backdoor results are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: The BRCA1 experiment flips labels only in a targeted protein domain; it does not use random label corruption or report training error.
